title: Predator in the Name of the Dead

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Predator in the Name of the Dead makes observation an ecological responsibility.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its machine narrator begins by confessing contamination of an inhabited alien world.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel connects pollinators, parasites, inherited memory, and the limits of understanding.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its distinctive tension lies in learning about lives already changed by the observer.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its ecology makes memory and identity part of material interdependence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader enters through a confession, not a promise of neutral exploration.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Nymba's immense bell-shaped flowers respond to rain through sound.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Pollinating beyri match those vibrations as they move through the canopy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel first makes their environment legible as a working relationship.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their wax citadels and biological inheritance extend that relationship into civilization.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A parasite's presence complicates what the machine believes it has understood.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This opening rewards attention to bodies before assigning familiar moral roles.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The narrator's report begins with a minute deviation in a probe's mass.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its significance emerges across years rather than inside the initial measurement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That delay makes error and responsibility difficult to separate from interpretation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel joins ecological observation with the structure of a retrospective confession.
